proof_summary: After reversing the rows, the proof establishes—starting from a finite base case and preserving a stable run-boundary pattern—that the relevant sums and iterated run-length counts form an eight-coordinate vector evolving by a fixed nonnegative linear recurrence. Coordinate domination then gives submultiplicativity of the shifted row sums, so Fekete’s lemma applied to their logarithms yields convergence of their nth roots, and the fixed index shift is asymptotically harmless.
